summary: Self-hosted runners unable to upload job artifacts after storage service-account key rotation
summary_details: After a scheduled rotation of the GCS service-account JSON key in Vault, a subset of self-hosted release runners started failing artifact uploads with 403/permission errors. New jobs can start, but steps that persist artifacts to GCS fail consistently on affected runners.
impact: Several release pipelines (mainly canary and nightly builds) are failing at the artifact upload step. End-to-end CI completes for ~60% of jobs; ~40% fail depending on runner pool. This is impacting release cadence for two teams and blocking one canary rollout.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule a job on an affected self-hosted runner pool (label: release-runner). 2) Run a job that produces artifacts and pushes to GCS via the platform artifact uploader. 3) Observe upload step fail with 403 and 'permission denied' in upload logs.
observed_logs:
upload_error: google.api_core.exceptions.Forbidden: 403 The caller does not have permission
  at artifact_client.upload (uploader.go:142)
  Runner agent logs: token refresh ok; vault fetch success; gcloud auth activate-service-account failed with: 'invalid_grant' in a small subset of requests.
initial_hypothesis: Rotation of the GCS service-account key introduced a timing window where some runner agents kept a cached, now-revoked credential and attempted to use it to obtain short-lived tokens; cluster-level RBAC or IAM binding change might have been applied concurrently, causing inconsistent permission sets across runner pods.
investigation_notes: - Vault rotation job executed 2026-03-12T03:10Z and wrote new key:ss: gcs-release-sa. - We observed two behaviors: (A) runners that restarted after rotation pick up new key and succeed; (B) runners that continued running show vault fetch success but gcloud auth operations intermittently fail with 'invalid_grant' or 403 when exchanging keys. - No global IAM role changes detected in cloud audit logs at rotation time. - Artifact uploader config unchanged. - Affected runner pods share the same node pools as healthy ones; not a node-level network issue. - Related Slack thread: #ci-ops (link). - Linked issue INT-48917 (ephemeral-runner-vault-rewrap-decrypt-failure) investigated vault rewrap before; not identical but useful for pattern comparison.
reproduction_attempts: We reproduced the failure by running a small job on a pre-rotation runner (did not restart runner), confirming that artifact upload fails until runner process is restarted. Restarting the runner agent pod resolves the error in reproduced runs.
short_term_workaround: - Restart runner agent process on affected hosts (kubectl rollout restart daemonset/release-runner-agent) to force a fresh VAULT fetch and re-auth. - For critical release pipelines, temporarily route jobs to runner pools that have been rotated and restarted. - Notify teams of transient failures and recommended rerun after restart.
proposed_fix: 1) Patch the runner agent to detect service-account key rotation events in Vault and automatically re-auth without a full pod restart (hot-reload). 2) Add a post-rotation orchestrator step that performs a rolling restart of runner agents after a key rotation completes. 3) Add end-to-end test in rotation pipeline to validate artifact uploads after key rotate.
rollout_plan_and_risks: - Implement hot-reload in agent (small binary change) and ship to staging. - Run key rotation in staging and validate. - Deploy to prod behind a staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with monitoring. Risks: if hot-reload has an edge-case, some agents may still require restart; fallback is rolling restart orchestrator.
mitigation_done: - Performed targeted rolling restart of release-runner-agent on 8 affected hosts, which restored artifact uploads for ~95% of failing jobs. - Updated rotation runbook to include mandatory runner agent restart step until hot-reload is implemented.
resolution_eta: Hot-reload agent patch target: 2026-03-20. Complete rollout and rotation automation update by 2026-03-24.
follow_up_actions: - (OWNER: DevInfra) Implement agent hot-reload and add unit/integration tests (PR TBD). - (OWNER: CI Ops) Update rotation runbook to include canary restarts and validation job. - (OWNER: Security) Review rotation procedure to ensure zero-window guarantees if possible. - Create postmortem if production impact > 4 hours.
notes: Customer-impacting? Internal only. Affected teams: Release Eng, Platform, Security. Logged to #ci-ops and #incidents. Will escalate to SEV1 if more than two release pipelines are blocked beyond 6 hours.
